meta.title: Ocomenu — remove Finder's built-in right-click items on your Mac
meta.description: Ocomenu replaces Finder's right-click menu with one you choose the items of. Hide Get Info, Rename, Compress, Quick Look and the other built-in items no setting can remove, reorder them, and add your own. Free and open source.

hero.title: Finder's right-click menu, written by you.
hero.lead: Apple's items in Finder's context menu can't be removed — not in Settings, not with any Finder extension. Ocomenu serves its own menu in their place, so every line is up to you.

items.name: Hide the built-in items
lines: Get Info, Rename, Compress, Duplicate, Make Alias, Quick Look, Copy, Share…
The ones no setting and no Finder extension can take away
Items Finder would grey out for that file stay hidden, as in Finder

items.name: Arrange them your way
lines: A settings window modelled on Finder's own Customize Toolbar
Drag an item into the menu to add it, out of the menu to remove it
Separators as many as you like

items.name: Add your own
lines: Run a shell script — the selected paths arrive as "$@"
Open with an app of your choice
Copy or move to a folder, with " 2" added on a name clash, as Finder does

items.name: Finder's original, any time
lines: Hold ⌘ while right-clicking and Finder's own menu comes back for that click
Quit Ocomenu and everything is as it was

items.name: Finder left untouched
lines: Nothing is injected into Finder and nothing about Finder is changed
Ocomenu catches the right-click before Finder does and shows its own menu
Choosing a built-in item presses the same command in Finder's menu bar

setup.title: Before you order

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Download the DMG and drag Ocomenu into Applications, or use Homebrew.

steps.title: Let it open
steps.body: The author is not a registered Apple developer, so the first launch is blocked. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

steps.title: Allow Accessibility
steps.body: Ocomenu needs it to catch the right-click and to see what is under the pointer. Switch Ocomenu on in the list it opens.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.body: Open Ocomenu again, or click its menu bar icon, to arrange the menu. Right after installing it matches Finder's, so nothing disappears until you say so.

setup.note: Your own items ask for Automation access to Finder the first time they run, to learn which files are selected.

price.title: The bill
price.body: Open source under the MIT license. No account, no analytics in the app, nothing sent anywhere.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Ocomenu shows its own menu when you right-click in Finder. It has no server, no analytics, and no account.

sections.title: What it reads
sections.body: When you right-click in Finder, Ocomenu reads which file or folder is under the pointer and whether it is selected, through macOS's Accessibility interface. It looks at clicks only while the pointer is over Finder, and it does not record them.

sections.title: Your own items
sections.body: Items you add ask Finder which files are selected and hand those paths to the script, app or folder you chose. That happens on your Mac only.

sections.title: Nothing leaves the Mac
sections.body: Your menu is saved in the app's preferences on your Mac. Nothing is collected or uploaded.

sections.title: Update checks go to GitHub
sections.body: Once at launch, Ocomenu downloads a small file from GitHub to see whether a newer version exists. GitHub receives the request like any download; Ocomenu sends nothing else with it.

sections.title: This website
sections.body: This page uses Vercel Web Analytics, which counts visits without cookies and without identifying you.

sections.title: Questions
sections.body: Open an issue on the GitHub repository.
